 Keenan Allen is the newest member of the 49ers
 The 49ers traded a sixth-round pick in the 2027 draft for Keenan Allen
 by Kyle Posey Updated Nov 10, 2026, 6:56 PM UTC Facebook 
 Link 
 The San Francisco 49ers have traded for wide receiver Keenan Allen. It’s the second time the team has made a trade with the Indianapolis Colts. The compensation was a 2027 6th-round pick.
 So, a couple of weeks after the Niners couldn’t land Jauan Jennings, they went after a similar body type and veteran in Allen, who is 34.
 Allen has 40 receptions for the Colts this season for 351 yards and a touchdown. He’s lined up primarily on the outside in Indy, but the 49ers love condensed splits. Allen has lined up in the slot on 26% of his routes this season.
 During Monday’s conference call, Kyle Shanahan was asked about the last wide receiver the Niners traded for, Emmanuel Sanders, and how he got acclimated into the offense so quickly:
 “Where he was in his career. He was the number one receiver for the Broncos at the time, had been for the prior four years and was still at that part in his career. He wasn’t just sitting there available on the street. He was the number one receiver on another team who was out of contention and he was looking to go somewhere else. So, it was just different spots.”
 Allen is long removed from being a No. 1 receiver, but longevity in the NFL should allow him to find his way quicker than most would in the 49ers offense.
 Per Next Gen Stats, Allen was the only Colts receiver with at least 50 routes run to post a yards-per-route above league average.
 Allen’s air yards per target is the lowest it’s been since 2017. On targets under 10 air yards, Allen has caught 31 of his 38 targets for 230 yards and a touchdown. That’s the seventh-most yards among all wide receivers under 10 yards.
 The 49ers average 5.29 yards to go on third down. That’s first in the NFL. To me, this is the Niners giving themselves a reliable veteran option underneath on third down. Allen has a couple of drops this season, but 50% of his targets result in a first down, despite a low depth of target.
 Injuries have decimated the 49ers this season. Mike Evans has missed two games in a row and is expected to miss a third. Deebo Samuel will return after missing three games. Christian Kirk made it one game before landing on the Injured Reserve. De’Zhaun Stribling didn’t make it out of Week 1. He’s expected to return before the end of the season. And Ricky Pearsall never made it to the regular season.
